answer_as_filed:
How 340B Savings Support MetroHealth Patients:
 
The MetroHealth System is Cuyahoga County's public safety-net health system, caring for more than 300,000 patients regardless of their ability to pay. MetroHealth participates in the 340B Program with services provided through two types of covered entities: MetroHealth Medical Center, a disproportionate share hospital (DSH), and MetroHealth Community Health Centers, a federally qualified health center (FQHC). The benefits described below reflect the coordinated work of both covered entities to provide comprehensive patient care services to the region. Public hospitals and Community Health Centers like ours care for the community's most medically and socially vulnerable, low-income residents. They are exactly the providers Congress intended to benefit when it created the 340B Program. MetroHealth Medical Center was the second hospital in Ohio to join the program, in early 1994.
 
Our patients face barriers to health that extend well beyond the exam room: 22% experience housing instability, 22% face food insecurity, 13% deal with transportation insecurity, and 17.5% live below the federal poverty level. More than two-thirds rely on government insurance programs like Medicaid or Medicare, or are uninsured.
 
340B savings allow MetroHealth to stretch limited resources further and reinvest them in care and services that would otherwise be reduced or unavailable. Most importantly, the program lets us bring life-saving medications and outpatient care to the neighborhoods where our patients live. That keeps people out of the emergency department and lowers the risk that their conditions become life-threatening. Because of 340B, MetroHealth is:
 
• Making medications affordable: MetroHealth offers four levels of financial assistance for Cuyahoga County residents with incomes up to 400% of the federal poverty level. These plans provide comprehensive care, including prescription drugs, at no cost or at a steeply discounted cost. Patients who don't qualify can receive vouchers and copay assistance to lower what they pay at the pharmacy. Our financial assistance coordinators also help any patient find lower-cost medications, manufacturer assistance and other programs. They also help patients get specialty drugs for cancer, HIV, hepatitis C, rheumatologic and cardiovascular conditions at affordable prices. Last year, that work saved patients more than $52 million. And because our pharmacy prices average 25–30% below other retail pharmacies, we lower costs for payers as well.
 
• Getting patients on treatment faster: For specialty and high-cost medications, insurance approvals are often what delays care. MetroHealth's Specialty Pharmacy and centralized prior authorization call center take that work on. They handle insurer requirements, secure approvals and find financial assistance. In 2025, the team completed 54,250 prior authorizations with an average turnaround of about 18 hours. Patients start therapy sooner and stay on it, and our providers can spend their time treating patients instead of doing paperwork.
 
• Bringing care into the neighborhoods: Our more than 20 outpatient locations across Cleveland and Cuyahoga County offer primary and specialty care, dental, vision and behavioral health services for all ages. Patients who qualify receive this care free or at significantly reduced cost. These sites keep people healthy and out of the hospital, but the network runs at a significant financial loss, which 340B savings help offset.
 
• Expanding pharmacy access: MetroHealth operates twelve community retail pharmacies in neighborhoods where our patients live, including areas that became pharmacy deserts when chain pharmacies closed. These locations offer free vaccinations and no-cost home delivery. At our main campus, a 24/7 pharmacy with drive-through service is open to anyone in the community who needs medication after an Emergency Department visit, after hours, or when other pharmacies are closed.
 
• Putting pharmacists on the care team: MetroHealth embeds pharmacists in clinical areas as part of our inpatient and ambulatory care teams. There they work directly with patients and adjust treatment as needs change, improving health outcomes.
 
• Sending patients home with their medications: Our bedside delivery program brings prescriptions to patients before discharge, so they don't need an extra trip to the pharmacy. No-cost home delivery continues after they get home. For patients with transportation, mobility or other barriers, this makes it far more likely they start and stay on their medications. That helps prevent complications and avoidable return visits to the hospital. Delivery also supports our antimicrobial stewardship efforts. When culture results or clinical review show that a patient needs a different antibiotic after discharge, our pharmacy team coordinates the change and delivers the new antibiotic to the patient's home the same day.
 
• Supporting mothers, babies and families: MetroHealth partners with the community to improve maternal and infant health and reduce infant mortality. 340B savings have helped expand access to midwives and doulas, home visits through our Nurse-Family Partnership team, and CenteringPregnancy programs that support pregnant women early and often throughout pregnancy.
 
• Keeping care going through crises: 340B resources helped MetroHealth maintain access to medications and uninterrupted care through major disruptions. These included the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack, which disrupted pharmacy services nationwide.
 
• Caring for patients who have nowhere else to turn: In 2025, MetroHealth provided $358 million in charity care, nearly $1 million every day. 340B savings give a public safety-net system the financial flexibility to keep offering Level I trauma care, adult and pediatric burn care, primary and specialty care, and other essential services to everyone, regardless of ability to pay.
 
Without 340B savings, MetroHealth would have far fewer resources to sustain these services, and the impact would reach well beyond the pharmacy counter. Financial assistance, neighborhood clinics, pharmacy access and the programs that help patients overcome barriers to care would all come under pressure. For many of our patients, 340B is the difference between getting care close to home and getting care only in an emergency room.
